clue.text: Close to the batsman, Bunter looks a fool

parts.note: silly is the cricket prefix for fielding positions very near the batsman, as in silly point
Billy Bunter is the greedy schoolboy of Frank Richards's comic stories

explanation.surface: A fielder crouching near the batsman is mocked as an idiot by the chubby schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: SILLY in cricket names the close-in fielding spots (silly point, silly mid-on); Billy Bunter is a famous fat schoolboy of British comic fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly billy is a gently mocking British phrase for a foolish person.

clue.text: Herb, a wise man

explanation.surface: A plant and a learned elder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is a culinary plant, and also a person of great wisdom.

clue.text: Looking round, see shelter ahead

indicators.note: ahead places the word for shelter in front of the round word

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a ring is round, a circle

explanation.surface: Glancing about, I spot cover just in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Leering is looking at someone slyly or lasciviously.

clue.text: American eye looked,..and .turned aside

indicators.note: turned aside means the letters of the words before are diverted into a new order

explanation.surface: A US citizen's gaze wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: YANKEE DOODLE, from the song, stands for any American.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee Doodle, from the old song, is a nickname for an American.

clue.text: At home I left unknown wickedness

parts.note: in means at home
quit means left, departed
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Staying in, I abandoned some unspecified wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is grossly immoral behaviour or sin.

clue.text: The French coast has no southern city

parts.note: la is the French for the

indicators.note: has no means the coast word loses its letter for southern

parts.note: a shore is a coast

explanation.surface: France's coastline has no city in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is a major city in Pakistan, the capital of Punjab province.

clue.text: Auguring man of Semitic origins

parts.note: an auguring man foretells the future, so a prophet, and one of Hebrew stock: a minor prophet of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A soothsayer whose roots lie among the Semitic peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos was a Hebrew prophet whose book is among the Old Testament's minor prophets.

clue.text: Revolutionary greeting in an eastern tongue

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A rebel says hello in an Asian language.
explanation.definitionFit: Marathi is an Indian language spoken chiefly in Maharashtra.

clue.text: Second convenient bloomer, we hear, produces a drink

parts.note: handy means convenient

indicators.note: we hear says the blunder word is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a bloomer is a blunder or gaffe

explanation.surface: Another handy flower, apparently, yields a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a flower but is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandygaff is beer mixed with ginger beer or lemonade, the original shandy.

clue.text: The niggler who's arranged to go

explanation.surface: A fussy pedant has organised permission to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb but is a noun: the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving the green light, after the traffic signal, means granting the go-ahead.

clue.text: Girl mislaying her first song

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman has misplaced the first song she had.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Fluency it bestows enables try on to come off

indicators.note: coming off means the letters of these words are knocked loose and reassembled

explanation.surface: The gift of the gab lets an attempted trick succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blarney Stone, at Blarney Castle in Ireland, is said to grant eloquence to those who kiss it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing this stone at an Irish castle is said to give the gift of the gab.

clue.text: Eat when girl comes back

indicators.note: comes back tells us the girl's name is written backwards

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Dinner is served once the daughter gets home.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to have a meal.

clue.text: Not told outside the family

explanation.surface: A secret kept from those who are not kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrelated can mean not narrated or recounted, and also not connected by kinship.

clue.text: Harris's character in Lewis's unfinished book, right? Mistake!

indicators.note: in puts the letters for right and mistake inside the shortened title
unfinished means the title loses its final letter

parts.note: Babbitt is the satirical novel by Sinclair Lewis, the Lewis named
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A figure from one author misplaced in another's incomplete novel: correct? An error!
explanation.walkthrough: Joel Chandler Harris wrote the Uncle Remus tales; 'unfinished' trims BABBITT to BABBIT, and 'in' places R and ERR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brer Rabbit is the trickster hero of Joel Chandler Harris's Uncle Remus stories.

clue.text: Stiffness not following on chill

parts.note: frigidity is coldness or chill
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Rigor that comes not from what follows but from cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigidity is inflexibility, the quality of being hard to bend.

clue.text: It's difficult to get right inside drawing

indicators.note: inside says the letter for right goes into the word for drawing

parts.note: tying a match means drawing it, ending level

explanation.surface: Sketching is hard if you have to get it exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests sketching but means drawing a game: TYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying means testing one's patience, so hard to cope with.

clue.text: Clergyman who will shortly finish the Bible

definitions.text: Clergyman who will shortly finish the Bible

parts.words: Clergyman who will shortly finish the Bible
parts.note: a minister's title is shortened to the same three letters as the Bible's last book, Revelation

explanation.surface: A minister is about to complete his reading of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title of a member of the clergy, abbreviated Rev.

clue.text: Foreign money order not in order

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An overseas money order has arrived jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means haphazard, lacking any pattern or arrangement.

clue.text: Screw up, endlessly trailing

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom upwards
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: dragging means trailing along behind

explanation.surface: Tighten the screw, and keep it dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' is old slang for a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a stingy person, as is a screw in old slang.

clue.text: Fabulous person — in retrospect, there are not many about more humble

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect means the whole construction is read backwards
about says the word for not many goes round the humbler word

parts.note: few means not many
lower means humbler, of more modest standing

explanation.surface: Looking back, few people are humbler than this storybook character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts FEW around LOWER to give FLOWEREW, and 'in retrospect' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf is a creature of fable, a man turning into a wolf.

clue.text: First opportunity

explanation.surface: A first chance.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is the first part of something, such as a chess game, and also a chance or vacancy.

clue.text: Many a woman exhibits spite

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
Alice is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Plenty of women show ill will.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to harm others, ill will.

clue.text: Sponge from financial backer and set

explanation.surface: Someone who funds a business and a firmly fixed sum are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel cake is a light, pale sponge made with egg whites.

clue.text: Did in turn

explanation.surface: Murdered someone, then spun round.
explanation.definitionFit: Slew is the past of slay, meaning killed, and also a verb meaning swing round.

clue.text: Encounter swarm when climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: to teem is to swarm, be crowded

explanation.surface: Bees meet as they swarm upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone is to come across them.

clue.text: Some, maybe, aren't meant to' be patient

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Perhaps some people simply aren't cut out for waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'meant to', but those words only link: the verb on its own means to be patient, as in 'bear with me'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure it calmly, putting up with it.

clue.text: Advise order to move — eg, eviction

explanation.definitionFit: To give notice of something is to inform someone of it formally.

clue.text: Widespread movement bound to make itself heard

parts.note: bound means tied up

explanation.surface: A broad movement is certain to get its voice across.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide is a general current of opinion or events, as in the tide of history.

clue.text: Did the wage turn out to be an encumbrance?

indicators.note: turn out says the letters of these words are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: Was the pay packet a burden in the end?
